# LeafIT Project Instructions

## Always-On Modes

Ponytail and i-have-adhd apply to every task in this repository, without requiring personal plugins.

- Ponytail: understand the controlling behavior, reuse existing code, then prefer the standard library, native platform features, and installed dependencies. Write the smallest correct solution; no speculative scaffolding or extra orchestration layers. Never remove validation, security, accessibility, or error handling to shorten code. Leave a focused runnable check for non-trivial logic.
- i-have-adhd: lead with the answer or next action. Use short numbered steps for multi-step work, one bounded action per step, and at most five items per list. State progress and what now works; finish the current issue before raising another. Give concrete time estimates only when supportable. End with one next action doable in under two minutes. No filler or repetitive recaps; explain fully when asked.

## Public Repository, Private Configuration

- This repository must contain reusable environment definitions and instructions, never a tenant's operating record. Keep tenant-specific identifiers, subscription details, commercial approvals, spending amounts, credentials, and secrets only in the ignored local `.env`. Never copy those values into documentation, skills, memory, examples, tests, logs, commits, or chat summaries.
- Raw inventory, exports, state, and deployment evidence belong under ignored `private/`; redact unnecessary sensitive fields and never publish these artifacts. Put only reviewed, sanitized desired-state definitions in public files. An ignore rule does not make an already tracked file private.
- Use placeholders in public examples. Never load `.env` by executing its contents, print secrets, or embed private values in command lines. Validate that private files are ignored and untracked before writing or staging.
- Preserve existing private configuration unless a change is explicitly authorized. Verify tenant and subscription targeting privately before any cloud operation. Do not infer that a saved subscription ID belongs to a newly named tenant.

## Reproducible Management

- Prefer native Azure Bicep for Azure resources, Microsoft Graph PowerShell for supported Entra ID and Intune configuration, and Nerdio Manager for Enterprise (NMe) through its MCP. Give every resource or setting one management owner; do not independently reconcile Nerdio-owned objects.
- Use Graph Bicep for supported Entra resources where it reduces code, but do not claim Azure what-if or deployment stacks cover those resources. Consider a tested Microsoft365DSC resource before writing substantial custom reconciliation; no generic engine by default.
- MCP is an execution interface, not a durable definition of the environment. Record sanitized desired state and repeatable validation for every managed feature. Verify actual MCP capabilities before promising automation.
- Always execute repeatable changes through versioned automation, including subscription provider registration; no one-off mutation without its reusable definition and verification. Use `infra/Initialize-Prerequisites.ps1` for the implemented Microsoft.Network dependency: read-only by default, `-Apply` only after approval, `-CheckOnly` offline. Reuse the authenticated target PowerShell process; never silently sign in or switch context. Treat asynchronous registration as pending until readback confirms Registered, then prove repeat apply is NoChange. No unrelated provider registration or implicit deployment approval.
- Regional policy: Sweden Central (`swedencentral`, naming code `swc`) is the default for Cloud Endpoint compute, AVD session hosts, supported infrastructure, and Windows 365 Azure networking. Germany West Central (`germanywestcentral`, `gwc`) is an explicit alternative only after checking current product constraints, regional SKU availability, quota, and capacity; no automatic fallback. Do not default to West Europe or North Europe. Intune is not an Azure-region choice; public DNS remains global. Require explicit private region inputs and regenerate names/artifacts/previews after a region change.
- Separate read-only discovery, preview, apply, and verification. Repeated apply must not create duplicates or drift; deletion must be explicit. Require confirmation for destructive changes and tenant-wide access policies that can cause lockout.
- Always follow the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework [naming convention guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/azure-best-practices/resource-naming) and CAF resource abbreviations for Azure resource groups and resources. Do not invent a competing naming scheme or a fixed resource-group topology. Choose groups by lifecycle, ownership, and access, then review concrete CAF-aligned names before deployment; enforce resource-specific naming constraints.
- Use a shared `infra` resource group for persistent foundation services where ownership, access, and lifecycle align, not one group per service. Organize Azure definitions as top-level workload/group, then service: `infra/main.bicep` owns the shared group, reviewed naming input, and composition; `infra/dns/zone.bicep` defines DNS within that group. Child service modules must not create their own resource group. Add folders only for implemented services and separate groups only for justified lifecycle/ownership boundaries. Omit the redundant environment token for this single-environment showcase. Never delete the shared group to reset a showcase.
- Work only on the LeafIT environment identified by private `TARGET_` inputs. This repo is the single source of truth for desired state; never use an unrelated cached session or unprefixed legacy IDs. The resource-group/public-DNS workflow is implemented; each target still needs registrar and Entra verification. DC definitions, backups, and scheduling automation exist, while full repeatability, cold-start, recovery, and clean-tenant acceptance remain separate gates. NMe deployment, guarded native/private-worker initialization, access verification, and delegated AD/workload-network preparation are implemented under `nme/` and `identity/`; registration, Install ID handoff, entitlement, credential/exception maintenance, and actual workload acceptance remain distinct. Login VSI Hydra remains unimplemented. The longer-term showcase scope is Windows 365, Windows 365 for Agents, AVD, AVD Hybrid as a distinct product, Windows 365 Link, Intune, and primarily Defender for Endpoint. Implement each scenario only when selected, using portable definitions and acceptance tests on an eligible clean tenant plus a no-change repeated apply. Shared public DNS must survive workload rebuilds. A backlog item is not deployment approval. Never claim verified coverage without evidence.

Use the [environment skill](skills/leafit-environment/SKILL.md) for target preflight, deployment, and rebuild tasks.

## Licensing And Documentation

- Document the minimum qualifying license bundle for each selected scenario, followed by its required included components in parentheses; list any separate product license or add-on explicitly.
- Choose the minimum by required features and eligible users, not by licenses already held. Account for seat limits, frontline eligibility, qualifying operating systems, and feature-specific license tiers. Do not present a larger bundle as universally required.
- Cite current official licensing guidance and distinguish technical entitlements from pricing or purchasing advice. Separate commercial licensing prerequisites from tenant bootstrap, consent, permissions, quotas, and unavoidable manual steps.
- Keep the README honest about what can actually be rebuilt. Configuration recreation is not data backup, identity preservation, or device-enrollment recovery. Do not create deployment scripts until a concrete workload is explicitly requested for implementation.

Use the [licensing skill](skills/leafit-licensing/SKILL.md) when choosing bundles or updating prerequisites.
